---
title: "Recommendations"
---

## For analysts reconstructing the study

Use model–legacy disagreement to prioritize employer-record review. Preserve the original label, proposed label, evidence and reviewer decision rather than silently overwriting the knowledge base. Distinguish name-extraction, entity-normalization and industry-attribute errors because their remedies differ.

Compare models against the actual operational objective. The paper favors GBDT for finding undefined employers, while the legacy system retains higher classification F-scores. An error-discovery model and a production labeler need not be the same system.

Audit agreement cases as well as flagged records. The paper's 97-of-100 agreement audit leaves evidence of residual error. A new study should budget for independent review across both groups.

## For a student career product

Before recommending a role, salary expectation or location, measure the selected pathway in a dated dataset. Use employer-industry checks to improve the sample, then compute market benchmarks and compare actual student profiles with explicit requirements.

The available evidence does not establish which roles are most promising, which skills a particular student lacks, or which remote locations are most realistic. Those recommendations remain dependent on the course extension. The [market](market.qmd), [skills](skills.qmd) and [evaluation](evaluation.qmd) pages define the necessary inputs and calculations.

## Next empirical milestone

Confirm one pathway and industry, obtain authorized posting data, and run the analysis in the assigned EC2 environment. Produce a filtering ledger and baseline before model tuning. Then add observed skill gaps, evaluated analytics and evidence-based recommendations to the site and report.
